correctness.rationale: Component degrees preserve the Fermat cubic and line divisor. The unique concurrence point gives a block form; coefficient comparison forces zero shear and equal cubic scaling. The binary cubic root set has projective stabilizer S3, with three lifts for each root permutation, yielding 18 elements. The unique fourth line not through the concurrence point cuts this group to three elements. The packaged verifier independently replays the explicit normal forms, kernel, complement, and D7 subgroup.

value.rationale: The two displayed arrangements are the explicit realized degree-six and degree-seven free examples in the lead classification. Exact embedded isotropy is a natural invariant of these configurations. The order-18 to order-3 drop explains quantitatively how one added flex tangent destroys the full S3 line-permutation symmetry while preserving freeness, and the central C3 identifies a hidden componentwise symmetry not visible from merely permuting the lines.
